specification.problem: Order finding for Shor's algorithm with N=15, a=2 (order r=4), with the ideal circuit and three assumed gate-imperfection models (systematic, random, combined) on the QFT controlled-phase gates. The aim is to compare the success probability with the ideal value and define an operational error threshold sigma_c.
specification.reconstruction_scope: One tiny instance: t=4 counting qubits, 4 work qubits, N=15, a=2. The unitary includes X on work qubit 0 to prepare y=1, H on the counting qubits, controlled modular multiplications, and an inverse QFT whose controlled-phase angles are perturbed by explicit numeric error values. Excluded: the paper's analytic threshold formula and precise error definitions, scaling with N beyond a numerical sigma_c, and classical decoding. The circuit covers only N=15 with a in {2,4,8,7,11,13} as a compiled permutation; the demonstrated instance is a=2. Decoding is documented but is not part of the unitary.

symbols.meaning: multiplicative order of a mod N
counting register integer, little-endian x=sum_k x_k 2^k
work register integer, little-endian, mod N
fixed systematic relative and absolute angle errors
random angle offset of phase gate j, zero mean, width sigma
probability mass on counting outcomes x with x/2^t within rounding of s/r
largest sigma with averaged P_succ >= eta times ideal

equations.label: Modular multiplication unitary
equations.description: Controlled modular exponentiation acting on work register initialized to y=1. For y>=15 the state is left fixed so U is a permutation. For a=2, U is a left cyclic rotation of the 4 work bits.
assumptions: Compiled with explicit classical a and N
Work register is 4 qubits, y=1 initially (X on work[0] required)

equations.label: Ideal output distribution
equations.description: Ideal outcome peaks at x/2^t near s/r. For t=4, r=4 peaks are x=0,4,8,12 with probability 1/4 each.
assumptions: r divides 2^t exactly in this instance

equations.label: Systematic error model
equations.description: The same fixed angle error is applied to every controlled-phase gate.
equations.justification: The abstract names systematic errors without defining them, so this is an assumed definition.

equations.label: Random and combined error models
equations.description: Independent random offsets per gate, or fixed offset plus random offsets. Several seeds are averaged.
equations.justification: The abstract names the three categories without definitions.

equations.label: Success probability and threshold
equations.description: Operational numerical threshold with cutoff fraction eta, e.g. 1/2.
equations.justification: The abstract says an error threshold is given for N but not its form; this is a stand-in.

equations.label: Ideal inverse QFT gate decomposition
equations.latex: \mathrm{QFT}^{-1}:\ \text{H on qubit } k \text{ and CP}(-\pi/2^{m}) \text{ between qubits separated by } m,\ \text{with bit-reversal swaps}
equations.description: Inverse QFT from H and controlled-phase gates with ideal angles -theta_m, which the error models perturb.

registers.name: work
registers.role: holds y mod 15, little-endian, initial value 1

specification.initial_state: |0>^4 on count; work register prepared to |0001> (y=1) by an X gate on work[0], included at the start of the unitary

steps.description: Apply X on work qubit 0 to prepare y=1. Without this the controlled multiplications act trivially on |0000>.
Apply H to every counting qubit, giving a uniform superposition over x.

Apply controlled U^(2^k) from counting qubit k onto the work register, U being multiplication by 2 mod 15 (cyclic bit rotation, via controlled swaps). Optionally add small Rz rotations after these gates.
Apply the inverse QFT on the counting register with swaps, with the controlled-phase angles perturbed per the chosen error model using explicit numeric values.
Outside the unitary: simulate the output distribution, check the ideal peaks at x=0,4,8,12, and evaluate P_succ against the ideal value and sigma_c, averaging over seeds for random errors.

specification.measurement: Measure the counting register in the computational basis, outside the built unitary.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Continued fractions of x/2^t give r, then gcd(a^(r/2)±1, N) gives factors. Compute P_succ against the ideal value and average over seeds for random errors.
assumptions: The error models are my definitions since the abstract does not define them
N=15, a=2, t=4 chosen as the smallest instance
The qualitative claim (robust to systematic, vulnerable to random errors) is only tested numerically on this single instance
missing_information: The analytic threshold formula as a function of N
The error distributions and gate set used by the paper
